claims.statement: An open changeset that is empty and whose last change is more than 24 hours old is discarded by housekeeping; an open changeset holding edits is never discarded by it, however long it sits idle.

prune_empty's UPDATE discards only rows with state 'open', updated_at < cutoff, and NOT EXISTS changeset_entries. Housekeeping calls it with cutoff = now - EMPTY_CHANGESET_HOURS (24). It is the only time-based changeset discard in housekeeping; user deletion's discard is a separate path, not idle-based.

verdicts.rationale: The executed test pins both halves of the claim: an old empty changeset is discarded, while a new empty one and an old one holding an edit stay open. The SQL makes "empty" (no changeset_entries) a condition of the prune. The README's "no edit within 24 hours" means this when read as "never written to"; the wording is clarified under #891.
